data.title: HF Sinclair Appoints Shawn J. Carsten as Chief Financial Officer
data.description:
HF Sinclair Corporation (NYSE and NYSE Texas, Inc.: DINO) (“HF Sinclair” or the “Company”) today announced the appointment of Shawn J. Carsten as executive vice president and chief financial officer, effective Jan. 1, 2027. Carsten currently serves as vice president of finance and chief financial officer of Golden Pass LNG, where he leads the company’s finance organization, with responsibility for financial planning and performance, accounting, business controls, tax, risk management and treasury. He joined Golden Pass in 2024.

“Shawn is a highly accomplished finance leader with deep experience across the energy value chain,” said Steve Ledbetter, incoming chief executive officer and president of HF Sinclair. “He brings strong financial and operational expertise and a proven track record of building high-performing organizations. I look forward to working closely with Shawn as we maintain capital discipline, execute our strategy and create long-term value for our shareholders.”

“I am excited to join HF Sinclair and work alongside a talented team with a strong portfolio of high-quality businesses,” said Carsten. “I look forward to working with the team to drive performance, maintain financial discipline and strategically allocate capital. HF Sinclair has a strong foundation, and I see significant opportunity to build on it and create sustainable long-term value for shareholders.”

About Shawn J. Carsten

Carsten brings extensive financial and business leadership experience across the energy value chain. Before joining Golden Pass LNG, Carsten held senior finance and business leadership roles during a more than 30-year career with Shell, including serving as chief financial officer of Shell Midstream Partners. In that role, he led financial reporting, regulatory filings, business and financial controls and financial strategy. Earlier in his Shell career, Carsten held leadership roles spanning refining, chemicals, manufacturing, supply and distribution, global logistics and digital transformation in the U.S. and internationally.

Carsten holds a Bachelor of Science in finance from the University of Colorado Boulder and a Master of Business Administration from Northwestern University.

About HF Sinclair Corporation

HF Sinclair Corporation, headquartered in Dallas, Texas, is an independent energy company that produces and markets high-value light products such as gasoline, diesel fuel, jet fuel, renewable diesel and lubricants and specialty products. HF Sinclair owns and operates refineries located in Kansas, Oklahoma, New Mexico, Wyoming, Washington and Utah. HF Sinclair provides petroleum product and crude oil transportation, terminalling, storage and throughput services to our refineries and the petroleum industry. HF Sinclair markets its refined products principally in the Southwest U.S., the Rocky Mountains extending into the Pacific Northwest and in other neighboring Plains states and supplies high-quality fuels to more than 1,850 branded stations and licenses the use of the Sinclair brand to more than 350 additional locations throughout the country. HF Sinclair produces renewable diesel at two of its facilities in Wyoming and also at its facility in New Mexico. In addition, subsidiaries of HF Sinclair produce and market base oils and other specialized lubricants in the U.S., Canada and the Netherlands, and export products to more than 80 countries.

data.title: Compass Pathways to Participate in 9th Annual Evercore Healthcare Conference on December 1
data.description:
Compass Pathways plc (), a biotechnology company dedicated to unlocking urgently needed new treatment options in mental health care, announced today that management will attend the 9th Annual Evercore Healthcare Conference on December 1, 2026 and will participate in a fireside chat at 3:25pm ET.

A live audio webcast of the fireside chat will be accessible at the following link: https://event.summitcast.com/view/FkwyWrnNgoveMhBfJS2NCC/We7ydUWZPZM5Wf4zVRNZnZ

A replay of the webcast will be accessible for 30 days following each event at the “Events” page of the Investors section of the Compass website.

About Compass Pathways

We believe mental health patients deserve the possibility of a better future. Compass Pathways plc () is a biotechnology company dedicated to unlocking urgently needed new treatment options in mental health care. Our initial focus is developing COMP360 psilocybin, a proprietary, investigational, synthetic psilocybin treatment under evaluation for treatment-resistant depression (TRD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). COMP360 is a potentially first-in-class treatment and has Breakthrough Therapy designation from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), as well as Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway (ILAP) designation in the UK for TRD. We are leading the world’s largest classic psychedelic clinical program in TRD, and building upon that robust foundation, we are executing a late-stage trial evaluating COMP360 for PTSD, another condition with high unmet need. Our goal is to advance treatments that move the field of psychiatry towards treatment options that offer rapid onset and sustained durability with infrequent dosing.

Compass is headquartered in London, UK, with a U.S. office in New Jersey.

We are driven by our purpose of unlocking pathways to be – opening futures filled with possibility. Together, we are on an ambitious journey toward enabling people living with mental health conditions to find clarity through self-discovery, because every journey needs a Compass.

data.title: Meta Agrees to Hold Off on Issuing New Stock Until Court Decision
data.description:
By Meghan Bobrowsky

Meta Platforms said it would wait to issue any shares of its new non-voting Class C stock until after a related court case plays out in Delaware this spring.

The company is facing a series of lawsuits brought by shareholders alleging Meta breached its fiduciary duty by approving a deal that investors deemed unfair.

The new class of stock, which has no voting power, is intended to fund Meta's AI bills at a time when the company is on the hook for $825 billion in future spending commitments. In a legal filing, Meta confirmed it would wait until the courtroom process plays out to make any moves.

The company previously said it planned to use the stock to establish an at-the-market stock offering program of up to $60 billion, potentially beginning in the first quarter of 2027. The new shares also gave Meta Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg a way to sell equity to potentially pay a California wealth tax without losing any voting power.

In a statement, a Meta spokesman said the company is "seeking a final determination as quickly as the court will allow," and that it would "vigorously defend" itself against the claims in the lawsuits.

Write to Meghan Bobrowsky at meghan.bobrowsky@wsj.com

data.title: Alibaba Earnings Rebound Sharply as AI Profitability Improves — Update
data.description:
By Tracy Qu

Alibaba Group recorded a surge in fiscal second-quarter profit as its AI profitability and e-commerce business improved.

The Hangzhou-based company has doubled down on artificial intelligence as a growth driver, a push that faces a new risk from heightened scrutiny about exports of chips to China. It has committed to spending more than $53 billion over three years to develop both the hardware and software that power AI.

Its success on that front holds the key to staying competitive amid challenges from other big tech companies and startups alike. But going all in on AI has proved a drag on profitability over recent quarters, putting pressure on Alibaba to deliver on its AI goals.

Its latest results look reassuring.

Alibaba said net profit tripled from a year earlier to 64.535 billion yuan, equivalent to $9.68 billion, for the three months ended September. Analysts polled by FactSet had expected 23.72 billion yuan. Revenue grew about 10% to 271.52 billion yuan, also better than market estimates.

Alibaba said higher net investment income and income from operations drove the profit gains.

The earnings beat comes as the Chinese technology titan prepares a Hong Kong listing for its chip unit, T-Head, that investors view as a major validation of its efforts to produce in-house semiconductors. The business could fetch a valuation of $85 billion, according to Nomura estimates.

Alibaba on Thursday said its new AI chip, Zhenwu V900, is scheduled for commercial release for the first quarter of 2027.

But Alibaba still depends heavily on externally sourced chips, making it potentially vulnerable to tightened export controls. Its stock has fallen about 10% this week since the U.S. move to tighten export rules of advanced American-made chips.

The U.S. said this week that Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Singapore and Brazil will be added to a list of countries subject to export restrictions, a step intended to prevent Chinese customers from accessing data-center capacity in those countries remotely.

"We see this as a negative development for China's AI cloud industry, as tighter access to advanced computing resources could constrain AI model training and slow cloud revenue growth," Nomura analysts said in a research note.

Daiwa analyst John Choi said a rerating of China's internet sector is unlikely until investors gain conviction in Alibaba and Tencent, which will likely be the first stocks to be added if investors increase their China exposure. Concerns about Alibaba's elevated AI investment might ease if cloud profitability improves, he wrote in a note ahead of the results.

The company appears to be delivering on that front, with cloud business adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, and amortization more than doubling in the three months ended September, thanks to revenue growth and better operating efficiency. Meanwhile adjusted Ebita for its core e-commerce business more than tripled as losses in the food-delivery business narrowed.

Alibaba Cloud's recurring revenue from external customers rose 67%, driving faster overall cloud revenue growth, with profitability improving significantly, the company said.

Adjusted net profit--a metric closely watched by analysts, as it reflects core business operation profitability--rose 92% to 19.91 billion yuan. The measure excludes the effects of share-based compensation expenses, investment gains and losses, some impairments and other items.

"As AI monetization continues to ramp up, we will maintain disciplined investments in AI capabilities with a focus on return on invested capital while targeting to achieve positive free cash flow," Chief Financial Officer Toby Xu said.

E-commerce business revenue rose 2% in the second quarter. Revenue from AI cloud and compute services jumped 53%, while AI labs and applications revenue climbed 51%.

Write to Tracy Qu at tracy.qu@wsj.com

data.title: TSX futures gain as oil, gold edge up; Anthropic debut in focus
data.description:
Futures tied to Canada's commodity-heavy stock index rose on Thursday as oil and gold prices recouped some losses, while investors awaited Anthropic's market debut due later in the day.

December futures on the S&P/TSX 60 index (SXFcv1) were up 0.43% at 5:52 a.m. ET (1055 GMT).

  • Gold gained on bargain hunting and short covering with spot gold up 0.4% after hitting a 14-month low in the previous session

  • Brent crude was little changed after edging up 0.2% earlier in the session, as worries about Middle East supplies amid attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz offset expectations for a surplus

  • Investors are closely watching for Anthropic's much-awaited debut after the Claude chatbot maker priced its IPO above the marketed range, pulling off the largest offering on record

  • Anthropic's IPO values the company at roughly $1.5 trillion on a fully diluted basis, with its first day of trading expected to serve as a key test of investor appetite for the AI sector

  • On Wednesday, Canada's main stock index fell more than 2% to a five-month low, as lower oil and metal prices triggered a selloff in the energy and materials sectors

  • Separately, Alberta, Canada's main energy-producing province announced new legislation aimed at enhancing protections for communities and landowners while still encouraging data center development and oil and gas growth

data.title: Sellas Life Sciences Shares Sink After Pricing Public Offering
data.description:
By Connor Hart

Shares of Sellas Life Sciences Group fell after the company announced the pricing of an underwritten public offering for $150 million of shares of its common stock.

The stock declined 22%, to $13.98, in premarket trading Thursday. Through Wednesday's close, shares have more than quadrupled year to date.

The biopharmaceutical company said late Wednesday that it will sell more than 11.5 million shares of its common stock for $13 apiece.

The company will also grant underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to about 1.73 million additional shares at the public offering price, minus discounts and commissions.

J.P. Morgan and TD Cowen are acting as the lead book-running managers for the offering, which is expected to close on Friday.

Write to Connor Hart at connor.hart@wsj.com

Under Rule 8.3(a) of the Code, any person who is interested in 1% or more of any class of relevant securities of an offeree company or of any securities exchange offeror (being any offeror other than an offeror in respect of which it has been announced that its offer is, or is likely to be, solely in cash) must make an Opening Position Disclosure following the commencement of the offer period and, if later, following the announcement in which any securities exchange offeror is first identified. An Opening Position Disclosure must contain details of the person’s interests and short positions in, and rights to subscribe for, any relevant securities of each of (i) the offeree company and (ii) any securities exchange offeror(s). An Opening Position Disclosure by a person to whom Rule 8.3(a) applies must be made by no later than 3.30 pm (London time) on the 10th business day following the commencement of the offer period and, if appropriate, by no later than 3.30 pm (London time) on the 10th business day following the announcement in which any securities exchange offeror is first identified. Relevant persons who deal in the relevant securities of the offeree company or of a securities exchange offeror prior to the deadline for making an Opening Position Disclosure must instead make a Dealing Disclosure.

Under Rule 8.3(b) of the Code, any person who is, or becomes, interested in 1% or more of any class of relevant securities of the offeree company or of any securities exchange offeror must make a Dealing Disclosure if the person deals in any relevant securities of the offeree company or of any securities exchange offeror. A Dealing Disclosure must contain details of the dealing concerned and of the person’s interests and short positions in, and rights to subscribe for, any relevant securities of each of (i) the offeree company and (ii) any securities exchange offeror(s), save to the extent that these details have previously been disclosed under Rule 8. A Dealing Disclosure by a person to whom Rule 8.3(b) applies must be made by no later than 3.30 pm (London time) on the business day following the date of the relevant dealing.

If two or more persons act together pursuant to an agreement or understanding, whether formal or informal, to acquire or control an interest in relevant securities of an offeree company or a securities exchange offeror, they will be deemed to be a single person for the purpose of Rule 8.3.

Opening Position Disclosures must also be made by the offeree company and by any offeror and Dealing Disclosures must also be made by the offeree company, by any offeror and by any persons acting in concert with any of them (see Rules 8.1, 8.2 and 8.4).

data.title: Mitie first-half profit and revenue rise ahead of £3.1bn OCS takeover
data.description:
In the six months to September end, operating profit before other items jumped 14% to £123.5m, with revenue 8% higher at £.29bn, including organic growth of 4%. Mitie said organic growth was driven by contract wins, projects and pricing, after a 4% impact from the loss of one notable public sector contract in the previous year.

Basic earnings per share before other items rose 9% to 6.2p and Mitie hailed a record order book of £16.4bn, up from £16.3bn. It also highlighted a record bidding pipeline, up 14% to £36bn, with more than 70% to be awarded in the next 18 months.

The operating profit margin before other items was up 20 basis at 4.3% and free cash flow improved to £105m from £52m.

Chief executive Phil Bentley said: "Mitie’s first half FY27 results show continued growth, further margin progression and improved free cash flow generation.

"Our FY25-FY27 Strategic Plan has established Mitie as a leader across Facilities Management, Facilities Transformation and Facilities Compliance, and we expect to deliver all of the targets we set in October 2023.

"There are substantial opportunities ahead to continue growing the business and increasing margins through our depth of customer relationships, our breadth of essential services and our technology and AI-enabled service delivery, underpinned by our record order book and bidding pipeline."

Mitie announced in July that it had agreed to be taken over by its private equity-backed rival OCS, after it offered to pay 218.5p for every Mitie share in cash plus a dividend of 3.1p per share. It said on Thursday that it continues to expect the deal to complete in the first quarter of 2027.

At 115 GMT, the shares were up 0.1% at 208.40p.
